name: Thomas Gainsborough
findings: Uses smoky black 1.8x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 724 paintings here).
Uses dark walnut 1.8x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 724 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, amber brown turns up as the lightest note in 57% of the paintings that hold it, 4.0x the archive's rate (from 724 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, taupe grey turns up as the shadow in 50% of the paintings that hold it, 4.0x the archive's rate (from 724 paintings here).
Pairs lavender grey with pale lilac grey more than chance would predict (3 of 724 paintings here).
Pairs biscuit with mushroom more than chance would predict (3 of 724 paintings here).
His single largest palette family (smoky black, dark walnut, dark olive brown) covers 76% of his paintings here.
Keeps 2 distinct palette families here, from smoky black, dark walnut to smoky black, dark chocolate brown.
